detail.why_its_a_bug: Deletes the 60KB content-size cap on kind:40008 diff events, allowing unbounded-size payloads through ingest.
Admission check now succeeds on every Ok result regardless of result.allowed, so rate-limit denials never take effect.

matched_by.claim: check_principal's match on the shared rate-limiter result has an unreachable second arm: the first arm `Ok(_) => Ok(())` catches every `Ok(RateLimitResult)` regardless of whether the limiter denied or allowed the request, so the `Ok(result) => Err(AdmissionError::Exceeded { .. })` arm beneath it can never run. Every principal-scoped admission check (WS event rate limiting in connection.rs, HTTP bridge admission in api/bridge.rs) therefore always succeeds as long as the limiter backend itself doesn't error, i.e. rate limiting on authenticated principals is effectively disabled.

detail.why_its_a_bug: is_verified() always reports true, so unverified events are treated as signature-verified.

matched_by.claim: StoredEvent::is_verified() is hardcoded to always return true, ignoring the struct's own private `verified` field that with_received_at() explicitly sets (and which defaults to false in new()). Any caller that trusts is_verified() as a gate for signature/id verification status will treat unverified events as verified.

detail.why_its_a_bug: Swaps NIP-10 e-tag markers so threadReference resolves parentId/rootId backwards.

matched_by.claim: In `NostrEvent.threadReference`, the local variables are assigned backwards: the tag whose NIP-01 marker is `'root'` is stored into `replyTag`, and the tag marked `'reply'` is stored into `rootTag`. The function then returns `parentId: replyTag[1]` (i.e., the value of the tag marked `'root'`) and `rootId: rootTag?[1]` (i.e., the value of the tag marked `'reply'`), which is the reverse of the intended NIP-10/desktop convention described in the comment two lines above.
